nodes.label: Observer-only guarantee
nodes.rationale: Scoping to observer-only (never deny/block tool calls, never modify input/output) avoids the trust burden, DSL/rules-engine complexity, and reputational risk of a control-plane plugin; trades enforcement power for adoption safety and a smaller engineering surface — the product competes on UX of visibility, not policy enforcement.

nodes.label: Superpowers SDD methodology (brainstorm → spec → plan → implement)
nodes.rationale: A linear, front-loaded spec-driven development lifecycle authored by the third-party obra/superpowers plugin; Throughline deliberately observes and visualizes this flow rather than forking or modifying it, to avoid coupling risk while still adding value.
nodes.norm_label: superpowers sdd methodology (brainstorm → spec → plan → implement)

nodes.label: Kanban layer (stories, backlog/in-progress/done)
nodes.rationale: A thin, opt-in continuous-flow board layered on top of Superpowers' single-work-item lifecycle, chosen over sprint-based Scrum because a solo developer plus an AI has no team to coordinate via ceremonies — standup and handoff are deliberately framed as context utilities, not rituals.

nodes.label: Phase inference (brainstorm/spec/plan/implement)
nodes.rationale: Best-effort mapping from InstructionsLoaded skill-load events and artifact presence to a lifecycle phase, since Superpowers exposes no structured phase state itself; the dashboard shows 'phase: unknown' rather than guessing badly, though the advisor review flags the heuristic as brittle (hardcoded skill names, monotonic/never-downgrading, no spec-detection branch).

nodes.label: Workflow Visualizer (Surface A)
nodes.rationale: Pairs Superpowers' own spec/plan markdown artifacts with the live hook-event stream so plan-checkbox progress, subagent activity, and phase are visible without repeatedly refreshing a markdown file in an IDE — positioned as the primary, always-on surface regardless of whether the optional Kanban layer is used.

nodes.label: Handoff / cross-session memory
nodes.rationale: The advisor review identifies this as the strongest, most defensible use case — Superpowers' own author has publicly stated cross-session memory is 'not wired up yet' — so persistent handoff notes that survive ephemeral Claude Code sessions fill a real, acknowledged gap rather than competing on telemetry depth.

nodes.label: Standup digest (context utility, not ceremony)
nodes.rationale: Auto-generated 'shipped yesterday / in progress / blocked' digest deliberately framed as a fast way to reload state into a fresh solo session, not a team-sync ritual, to avoid the 'Scrum for one' framing the advisor review warns against.

nodes.label: Story sizing (S/M/L)
nodes.rationale: T-shirt sizing kept deliberately simple and unenforced by the daemon (conventions documented in README/tooltips only); the advisor review notes it has no velocity feedback loop, so today it functions as decoration rather than real estimation data.

nodes.label: Scrum-vs-Kanban product framing critique
nodes.rationale: The advisor review's central verdict: the product is mislabeled — its Scrum-borrowed vocabulary (standup, story, sizing) sits over a mechanism that is actually continuous-flow Kanban wrapped around the linear SDD lifecycle of a single work item; dropping the Scrum label is judged the cheapest, highest-perception-impact fix.

nodes.label: DocsPage design contract
nodes.rationale: A versioned visual/CSS contract (tabs, markdown rendering, linked-card sidebar) shipped as a plugin agent skill so any future agent modifying the DocsPage reuses the shared design-token system instead of inventing a standalone style.
